steps.prompt: Without dividing, can $4735$ be shared equally into $5$ groups? Into $2$ groups? How do you know?

cards.title: Only the last digit matters
cards.body: Every number is some tens plus its last digit: $4735 = 4730 + 5$. Tens always divide by $2$, $5$ and $10$, so only the last digit decides. $4735$ ends in $5$: it divides by $5$, but not by $2$ or $10$.

cards.title: Worked example: remainders
cards.problem: What are the remainders when $638$ is divided by $10$, $5$ and $2$?

steps.text: $638 = 630 + 8$. By $10$ the remainder is the last digit.
By $2$: $8$ is even, so the remainder is $0$.

cards.title: Why it works
cards.body: Every ten is $2$ fives, or $5$ twos, so any number of tens shares exactly into $2$s, $5$s or $10$s. Whatever is left over has to come from the last digit.

prompts: Explain why the last digit is all you need to test for $5$.
